name: Rescue Method Performance Index (RMPI)
description: Rescue operations in abandoned and structurally compromised buildings represent a specific type of technical intervention in which the rapid evacuation of injured persons must be ensured while maintaining a high level of rescuer safety. The selection of an appropriate rope rescue method is influenced by multiple technical, organizational, and time-related factors, whose comprehensive assessment requires a systematic multi-criteria evaluation approach. The aim of this study was to develop a numerical model and to demonstrate its calculation procedure and internal applicability using data obtained from a case-specific full-scale rescue exercise. The proposed model is based on experimental data obtained during a full-scale rescue exercise conducted by members of the Fire and Rescue Service of the Slovak Republic, in which two casualty evacuation techniques—the Arizona Vortex Rescue System and the Improvised Rope Traverse System—were evaluated within the same predefined exercise scenario. Each method was performed once by the same five-member rescue team. The evaluation combined measured operational parameters, expert assessment of qualitative criteria, multi-criteria analysis, and criterion weighting using the Fuller pairwise comparison method. Because each rescue method was represented by a single trial, the observations do not permit an assessment of experimental repeatability or general comparative effectiveness.
